angle: DL/EDGE: Run-the-Hoop lateral force (Hoop G) as a tiebreak for pass rushers who skip the 3-cone; year-standardized; baseline = pick + weight + EDGE share + NGS score + official 10-yd split and 3-cone, fit leave-one-class-out and used as an offset
metric_name: Hoop G: peak half-second sideways acceleration (g) on the Run-the-Hoop curve, z within Combine year
headline_number: Held-out continuous test (beta-binomial, out-of-class forecast as offset, skeptical prior): +0.43 pressures per 100 rushes per sd of Hoop G [90%: 0.09, 0.77], n=78, positive in all 3 classes (0.23 / 0.21 / 0.09, each spanning zero); within-class shuffle p 0.003 but best-of-14 search-adjusted p 0.12. Frozen plus calls 4 of 9 vs 9 of 69, 0 of 2 in 2025. Lower-variance in-game outcome (1.5-s depth, reliability 0.85, tracks pressure rho 0.33) shows no Hoop G link: 0.5 in per sd [-0.9, 1.9], shuffle p 0.22.
what_changed_from_previous: DS: hit-count tests replaced as the headline by a continuous leave-one-class-out Bayesian slope with the no-tracking forecast as offset (per-class slopes with intervals, pooled slope, within-class shuffle null, held-out log score improved in 3 of 3); new lower-variance outcome from 10 Hz game frames (depth upfield 1.5 s after the snap; split-half reliability 0.85 vs 0.07 for sampled pressure; validated vs season pressure) tested with the same held-out design (null); direction-change rate tried (unreliable, null); rule frozen in frozen_rule.json with SHA-256 quoted; search-adjusted p 0.12 placed next to the headline p; one reconciled 3-cone table by class (43 official vs 45 tracked; 15 vs 14 in 2025). Football: Hoop G mechanism tested twice more and stated plainly as none, so the scout use is a tiebreak after the 3-cone and film; case table with film cut and cue for Johnson, Adebawore, Phillips, Black; scheme context from tracking (Phillips moved 2+ yd sideways by 1.5 s on 40% of sampled rushes in Miami vs 0% for Black in Pittsburgh's odd front); cost of a wrong call in picks (median 20), pressures and EPA; 2025 card with player-specific snap plans and film cuts. Writeup: plain lede around the title finding; coach-repeatable Hoop G definition; 'The ask' replaced by 'So what for a team' with three actions; power moved to Limitations; mid-p, twin, pick x rotation and the 27-variant paragraph removed from the body (one appendix row); pair test labelled post hoc in the appendix; 'Clearly below' column dropped. Viz: Fig 1 is a 7-player small multiple (3 hits, 2 2025 plus calls, Adebawore, Phillips) with narrow path panels, a wide interval column, and rushes and sampled counts per row; Fig 4 grid removed (one appendix row); Fig 2 gets a labelled binned calibration line, marked 2025 plus calls and a held-out 3-cone rho panel by class; new Fig 3 shows the held-out slopes and shuffle null for pressure and depth. Items go from 9 to 8.
open_risks: The pooled held-out slope (0.43, interval 0.09 to 0.77) is larger than every per-class estimate because the skeptical prior shrinks single classes harder; judges may read that as odd. It is explained in the Fig 3 subtitle only.
Hoop G was chosen as the best of 14 drills on the same seasons. Held-out classes test the forecast, not the drill choice, so the honest p is 0.12.
The 3-cone's out-of-class support (rho 0.36) rests on 8 rushers in 2025 and is negative in 2023 and 2024, which weakens 'the 3-cone decides first'.

The scheme context (stunt or slant rate, Pittsburgh's odd front) comes from about 20 sampled rushes and a 2-yard sideways proxy, not play calls; the card's snap plans and film cuts are judgment calls built on thin data.
The SHA-256 freezes the rule only from this commit on; there is no external timestamp yet.
